```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

format_table <- function(data, max_rows = 1000) {
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  row_count <- nrow(data)
  if (row_count > max_rows) {
    shown <- utils::head(data, max_rows)
    note <- paste("Showing first", max_rows, "of", row_count, "rows.")
  } else {
    shown <- data
    note <- paste("Showing all", row_count, "rows.")
  }
  list(table = shown, note = note, rows = row_count, cols = ncol(data))
}

report_y_range <- function(y_data, log_scale) {
  finite_y <- y_data[is.finite(y_data)]
  if (length(finite_y) == 0) {
    return(c(1e-12, 1))
  }

  if (isTRUE(log_scale)) {
    positive_y <- finite_y[finite_y > 0]
    if (length(positive_y) == 0) {
      return(c(1e-12, 1))
    }
    y_min <- max(min(positive_y, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.9, 1e-12)
    y_max <- max(positive_y, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
  } else {
    y_min <- min(finite_y, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.9
    y_max <- max(finite_y, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
  }

  if (!is.finite(y_min) || !is.finite(y_max) || y_min == y_max) {
    y_min <- 0
    y_max <- max(finite_y, na.rm = TRUE) + 1
  }

  c(max(y_min, 1e-12), max(y_max, 1e-12))
}

render_report_figure <- function(fig, simulation_output, num_ind, uploaded_observations = NULL) {
  fig_obs <- NULL
  if (!is.null(uploaded_observations) && "plot_compartment" %in% names(uploaded_observations)) {
    fig_obs <- uploaded_observations[uploaded_observations$plot_compartment == fig$plot_compartment, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  base_y_range <- report_y_range(fig$y_data, fig$log_scale)
  y_range <- range_with_user_observations(base_y_range[1], base_y_range[2], fig_obs, fig$log_scale)
  x_range <- range(0, max(simulation_output$time, na.rm = TRUE))

  par(oma = c(1, 1, 1, 1))
  par(mar = c(5, 6, 4, 2))
  plot_simulated_profile(
    simulation_output,
    fig$y_data,
    x_range,
    y_range,
    fig$log_scale,
    num_ind
  )
  axis(side = 1, cex.axis = 1.1)
  axis(side = 2, las = 1, cex.axis = 1.1)
  box()
  title(main = fig$title)
  mtext(side = 1, "Time [days]", line = 3, cex = 1.1)
  mtext(side = 2, fig$y_label, line = 4, cex = 1.1)

  sim_legend <- simulated_profile_legend(num_ind)
  user_legend <- plot_user_observations(
    fig_obs,
    sim_legend$labels,
    sim_legend$col,
    sim_legend$lty,
    sim_legend$pch,
    errorBars = TRUE,
    logScale = fig$log_scale
  )
  legend(
    "topright",
    legend = user_legend$labels,
    col = user_legend$col,
    lty = user_legend$lty,
    pch = user_legend$pch,
    lwd = 2,
    bty = "n",
    x.intersp = 0.7,
    seg.len = 1.4
  )
}
```

## Scenario Summary

- **Generated at:** `r params$generated_at`
- **Population simulation seed:** `r params$population_seed`
- **Model file:** `www/PBPK.cpp`

This report records the converted model parameters, generated dosing/input dataset, and simulation output needed to reproduce the selected scenario.

<p class="zip-note">The CSV files for this report are included in the downloaded ZIP file. After extracting the ZIP, open the CSV files from the same folder as <code>report.html</code>.</p>

## Converted Model Parameters

<p><span class="included-file">parameters.csv is included in this ZIP file</span></p>

```{r parameters-table}
parameter_table <- format_table(params$parameters, max_rows = Inf)
knitr::kable(parameter_table$table)
```

## Generated Input Dataset

<p><span class="included-file">input_dataset.csv is included in this ZIP file</span></p>

```{r input-data-table}
input_data_table <- format_table(params$input_data, max_rows = 20)
cat(input_data_table$note, "\n\n")
cat("Dimensions:", input_data_table$rows, "rows x", input_data_table$cols, "columns\n\n")
knitr::kable(input_data_table$table)
```


## Simulation Figures

<p class="report-figure-note">Figures are rendered in the report. Full numeric results are available in `simulation_output.csv`.</p>

```{r report-figures, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, results='asis'}
for (fig in params$figures) {
  cat("### ", fig$title, "\n\n", sep = "")
  render_report_figure(fig, params$simulation_output, params$num_ind, params$uploaded_observations)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Reproducibility Notes

For population simulations (`Number of individuals` > 1), use the listed population seed and retain the generated input dataset above to reproduce that exact population scenario.
